hyps.why: With edge 0 removed, node 1 gets no input, so a conv on edge 1->3 adds nothing.
Node 1 is disconnected from the input when edge 0 is none, so the edit is nearly inert.
Edge 1->2 carries no signal when node 1 has no input, so the conv is wasted.
Node 1 is dead without edge 0, so edge 2 edits have little effect.
Adding a conv where there was no direct input-to-output edge gives a large gain, more than replacing a useful op.
Replacing a strong skip path with a conv gains less, or even loses accuracy, compared with the average replaced op.
Filling an empty final edge with a conv adds a lot, while replacing an existing op adds less.
Restoring a removed edge into the output with a conv gives a bigger gain than swapping ops.
Reconnecting node 1 with a conv enables all downstream paths through node 1, a bigger gain than swapping ops.
With edge 1 removed, node 2 is fed only through the longer path 0->1->2, so a conv on edge 5 helps less.
